title: Empty Placeholder Trait Implementations (Do-Nothing Defaults)
pattern: Implementing empty method placeholders or dummy default values purely to satisfy a compiler trait requirement, leaving silent, inactive logic paths.
why_bad: It violates the expected behavior of the interface. Callers assume the mock or stub operates correctly, but calls are silently swallowed, masking errors and making system debugging extremely difficult.
detection: Trait implementations containing methods with empty bodies (`{}`) or returning hardcoded dummy literals with no active logging or assertion tracking.
counterexample: Intentionally designed null-objects or default traits that are explicitly documented to perform no actions (such as `std::default::Default`). `Context-dependent`.
